title: Capture direct workspace snapshots and enforce assignment path ownership
goal: Make the workspace state used for production and checking content-addressed, and allow only work whose effective access and path ownership are enforceable.
scope: Implement trusted WorkspaceGuard.open(Direct), lock(Read/Write), snapshot and release(assignment,basis) over a Direct WorkspaceProvider. Record workspace IDs, canonical relative paths, digests and release basis. Release conflicting access only after attributable cessation or never-started evidence; cessation may follow termination or effective withdrawal of access.

Retain snapshot content needed for later before/after checks, immutable results and finalization. Keep artifact bytes/content references under explicit application storage ownership; a digest without recoverable content is insufficient for rerunning a snapshot.

Replace invocation-wide blanket scope exclusivity with model path ownership: overlapping writes conflict, safe reads coexist where actual access permits, and declared disjoint paths are not treated as proof that a broad native writer is confined. Handle aliases, ancestor paths and symlink escapes according to effective capabilities.
acceptance: A real temporary filesystem consumer captures a before snapshot, observes changed bytes and reopens both exact snapshots after journal restart; subsequent workspace edits cannot change earlier snapshot content.

Concurrent compatible reads/disjoint enforceable writes succeed, overlapping or escaping writes are denied with owner references. A backend with broader effective write access cannot gain artificial parallelism from a narrower declared path list.

Direct and a substantially different constrained WorkspaceProvider run through WorkspaceGuard. Revoked/disconnected work retains conflicting holds until validated cessation or non-execution, while an unrelated scope remains usable. Reopened state retains the same release basis independently of cost settlement.
context: Authority: ymp-docs/self-organizing-team-domain-model.md, sections 3.2 (Snapshot, Artifact), 3.4 (Workspace, PathLock), 4 (WorkspaceGuard), 5.7 (WorkspaceProvider), principle 13 and R-9/R-16. Use the approved model with 811a872 semantics and the greenfield baseline in 0c61ff1 and §5.8 for experimental strategy boundaries. Other documents and existing names explain implementation facts only.

Greenfield: create this behavior in the new implementation. Paths below are PROPOSED target modules under the layout owned by W1-0001; only completed prerequisite tasks supply implementation. Prior source, APIs, fixtures and delivery claims are not a baseline.

Create proposed crates/ymp-domain/src/workspace.rs, crates/ymp-kernel/src/workspace_guard.rs and crates/ymp-runtime/src/workspace/direct.rs. W1-0016 supplies durable content storage; W1-0003 supplies explicit actual-capability facts. Implement Direct snapshot/path ownership as new behavior.

W1-0006 binds locks to admitted assignments; W1-0017 supplies native cessation observations, and W1-0008 submits ResultVersion from retained snapshots. This task tests WorkspaceGuard operations over attributable ownership/basis fixtures, not a fabricated completed agent result. IsolatedCopy/CopyOnWrite/merge are W4-0001.

Under §3.9/R-19, revocation, parent exit or stream loss alone cannot release conflicting access. Validate scoped cessation or never-started evidence; effective withdrawal of access may establish cessation. Financial settlement is independent and unrelated scopes can continue. Observation types remain implementation choices.

Implementation checkpoints: ymp-docs/workspace-implementation.md. Direct retained snapshots are committed in e1707a9. The current ownership checkpoint adds physical PathObservation, opaque scope/cessation inputs, WorkspaceGuard lock/authorize/revoke/release, LockChanged replay and aggregate conflict validation inside MemoryJournal/SQLite commit locks. Compatible reads and disjoint writes are tested with private synthetic evidence through the real consumer; cross-session/thread/process tests use Direct observations and trusted fixture events. These do not claim native confinement or cessation. Production access-evidence factories and the mediated alternative are not implemented.

Independent design review: native cwd is not confinement; an unconfined writer must be denied rather than given an artificial root scope. Path ownership needs physical/case/Unicode/ancestor alias treatment and one atomic coordinator across sessions/processes/stores. Holds persist after coordinator exit. A constrained alternative must mediate real operations and drain admitted operations before issuing withdrawal evidence. Direct double capture detects changes but is not an atomic filesystem snapshot; final check/result capture must be quiescent under the completed guard.

Ownership review ACCEPT after fixing orphan-head omission, requested-read capability enforcement and aggregate-history/control-capacity issues. SQLite inventories the union of heads/events/content links, rejects malformed session keys before loading strings, and retains only bounded active ownership from other sessions. All SQLite appends protect remaining authorization/revocation/release slots and bytes. Tests cover orphan owners, oversized keys, two-process conflict serialization, retained revocation and a small event limit that still permits authorize/revoke/release. Remaining integration work: protected physical-root binding across independent stores; actual mediated operations and drain-before-withdrawal evidence. Capture read holds are supplied by the following checkpoint. Keep W1-0005 in progress until these are implemented and independently accepted.

CaptureRead checkpoint: LockChanged starts an observed root Read hold with a per-attempt OS-random owner; SnapshotTaken v2 atomically publishes and ends it, or CaptureAborted records ended synchronous I/O without a snapshot. Bounded local completion evidence retries commit only, survives CAS/lost ACK within its Guard, and cannot be reconstructed by a fresh Guard for unresolved I/O. Failed foreign/absent begins are cleaned locally without aborting another owner, including deferred resolution after read unavailability. Historical SnapshotTaken v1 remains replayable/resolvable but cannot be newly appended; exact resolution still checks a complete preceding prefix. Independent review ACCEPT after nonce, prefix, cleanup and delta-replay fixes. Tests cover writer exclusion, completion faults without recapture, two Guard races including exact-match resolution, own lost begin ACK, abandonment, restart, historical replay and 64 local cleanup attempts in both read modes. Full W1-0005 still requires protected root binding and the actual mediated provider.

Root-binding checkpoint independently accepted and verified: SQLite format2 identity with transactional v1 migration preserves existing history/content; handles reject changed UUIDs, replaced files and hard links. Immutable root markers bind both logical and physical journal identities. WorkspaceGuard records WorkspaceBound; marker installation is no-replace and synchronized, nested bindings are refused, and copied stores cannot adopt the root. Unbound previews exclude bound descendants and block new descendant bindings during I/O; capture also checks caller identity under the provider binding mutex. Identity, root-binding, process/concurrency and full workspace checks passed. This does not supply execution authority: the actual mediated filesystem provider remains required before W1-0005 completion.
